title: run supervision: every run ends, and says why
intent: The most expensive failure of an agent is not the one that crashes but the one that continues: the run keeps asking the model, the model keeps asking for the same read, and the person's tokens and money go into a loop that nobody declared. This wave is supervision with visible teeth — a bounded number of visible nudges, a whole-run deadline, retries with backoff, and a doom-loop detector that does not punish a legitimate repeated read.
objection: A detector that stops a legitimate repeated read teaches the model that reading twice is forbidden, and the model then reads once and guesses — which is more expensive than the read.
refuted_by: A run of legitimate repeated inspection that the detector kills, or a run that exceeds its deadline without a terminal reason in the journal. One of the two is a bug in the supervisor.
